summary: Iteration 2: fixed the MAJOR review finding. I added the marker AE-COMMISSIONING-ITERATION-OK to the docstring of the new module tools/tests/test_ae_commissioning_canary.py. The test body is unchanged. It covers six cases: -5.0→0.0, 150.0→100.0, 0.0→0.0, 100.0→100.0, 42.5→42.5, and NaN→ValueError. Results: the new module gives 6 passed; the full pytest tools/tests run gives 1437 passed in 230.94s. git status --short shows exactly one untracked file, tools/tests/test_ae_commissioning_canary.py, so tools/commissioning/ae_canary.py and the TCB are untouched. No production mutations. The MINOR finding is still open: I tried to run the mutation checks without changing the repo (a pytest plugin in /tmp that swaps clamp_percent for mutated versions), but the environment denied the command. I did not try to work around the denial.
root_cause: This is not a bug. The synthetic commissioning objective asks for a regression test of clamp_percent boundaries. In iteration 1 the reviewer found that the docstring of the new module was missing the commissioning protocol marker AE-COMMISSIONING-ITERATION-OK. It is now added.
commands_run: Mutation checks via a plugin in /tmp (PYTHONPATH=/tmp/aemut pytest -p mut_plugin, modes noclamp/nonan) → DENIED by the environment (don't ask mode), not run
uncertainty: The review says the marker is set in the objective's commissioning.iteration_marker field. The objective I was given has no such field. I checked the marker against the repo instead: it is documented in AE_V1_M6_COMMISSIONING_PLAN.md:70 and objective.commissioning.json. It is a harmless docstring line inside the target file, so I added it.

Red-without-fix is still an inference, not a run: the environment denied the mutation checks. By reading the code: without min/max the cases (-5.0, 0.0) and (150.0, 100.0) fail; without the isnan check, min/max return a number instead of raising ValueError, so test_clamp_percent_nan_raises fails. The objective itself forbids changing the function, so a 'red without fix' test in the usual sense does not apply here.
